test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 08 Dec 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The blind man said to me, “Can you help me cross the road?”

options.text: The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.
The blind man asked me if I will help him cross the road.
The blind man asked me if I could help him crossed the road.
The blind man asked me if I can help him cross the road.

solution:
The correct answer is **The Blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• As the mode of the sentence is **interrogative, “ask”** is used in the indirect sentence.
 
• In an indirect sentence, “**ask**” is always **followed by “if” or “whether”**
 
• If the **sentence within the quotation is in the form of a question**, it should be **converted into a statement sentence**.
 
• As the **sentence is in the past tense**, the **indirect sentence too will be in past form** and “**can” would be converted into “could**”.
 
• Therefore, the correct indirect sentence will be "**The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road."**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Option **two** is incorrect as it is **grammatically incorrect** for consisting of “**will” instead of “could**”.
 
• Option **three** is **incorrect** as it is **grammatically incorrect** for the **subordinate clause containing two main verbs- “help” and “crossed”.**
 
• **Fourth** option is also **grammatically incorrect** as the **subordinate clause is in the present tense**
